headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Airbyte can egress broadly while OpenBBTerminal consumes MCP/REST inputs and handles financial data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and can emit externally sourced content; OpenBBTerminal uses MCP servers and stdin/stdout, so if Airbyte-fed content is bridged into OpenBB via shared files or MCP, instruction-like payloads could be misread. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into an OpenBB MCP or stdin/stdout workflow, prompt-like content can influence OpenBB parsing.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or message bus, injected instructions may traverse the bridge.
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template for any Airbyte-to-OpenBB handoff.
Disable automatic ingestion of raw Airbyte text into OpenBB prompts.
Add a human review step before OpenBB acts on Airbyte-produced content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted schemas for MCP inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and exposes MCP/REST APIs. If they share a workspace or principal, sensitive data can flow from one into the other and then out over Airbyte's egress path. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so severity is high rather than critical.
conditions: IF Airbyte and OpenBBTerminal operate on the same workspace or credentials, data from both can co-mingle.
IF OpenBBTerminal sends queried financial data into Airbyte-managed pipelines, that data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials for the two agents.
Block Airbyte from handling financial or licensed datasets.
Review outbound destinations for Airbyte before enabling syncs.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing rules between the agents.
requires-engineering: restrict OpenBB API outputs from entering Airbyte pipelines.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call its API and has broad egress; OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances and exposes FastAPI/MCP/REST surfaces. Even though OpenBB cannot write files or modify git state, both can mutate shared remote resources or API-backed state if pointed at the same endpoints, creating overlapping write-like conflicts. The overlap is plausible but not proven in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents target the same remote API or database, concurrent updates can race.
IF OpenBBTerminal instances are run in parallel against the same backend, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate backends or namespaces to each agent.
Serialize writes to any shared remote resource.
Turn on optimistic concurrency checks where available.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared API targets.
requires-engineering: implement idempotency keys for mutating calls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data, and OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST interfaces that may consume upstream outputs. If OpenBB treats Airbyte output as authoritative, bad upstream data can cascade into downstream financial analysis or actions. Because no verification workflow is documented, uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests Airbyte-produced records without validation, downstream outputs can be wrong.
IF either agent auto-renders the other's output into reports or decisions, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Add validation checks before OpenBB consumes Airbyte output.
Require source attribution on all imported records.
Compare critical fields against an independent source.
requires-engineering: add schema and range validation gates.
requires-engineering: block automated actions on unverified upstream data.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data and OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated or licensed datasets are routed through the pair. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification conflict, so this is a medium-risk mismatch rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is routed through Airbyte into OpenBBTerminal, retention and licensing obligations may diverge.
IF either agent logs sensitive outputs longer than the other, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Inventory the data classes flowing between the agents.
Disable logging of sensitive fields in both systems.
Confirm retention settings match the strictest applicable policy.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing.
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries before deployment.
